sec04-card-sec04-F42.front: Why must you never drink alcohol while taking other drugs or medications?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.expected_back: Never drink alcohol while taking other drugs, because they can multiply alcohol's effects or add effects of their own.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: Which four driving skills suffer under both legal prescription medicines and illegal street drugs?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.memory_hook: Both dull reflexes, sight, judgment, alertness
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Prescription and illegal drugs can both affect reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness in ways similar to alcohol.

sec04-card-sec04-F43.front: How do intense feelings disrupt driving, and what should you do when angry or worried before a trip?
sec04-card-sec04-F43.memory_hook: Cool off first or swap drivers
sec04-card-sec04-F43.expected_back: Strong emotions interfere with thinking, attention and processing information, so if you are angry or worried, cool off first, perhaps with a short walk or nap, or let someone else drive.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: Is anger the only feeling that ruins safe driving, and what is the safest move during intense emotion?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.memory_hook: Any extreme emotion means stay parked
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: Extreme levels of any emotion, not only anger, can keep you from driving well, and staying off the road until symptoms pass is the safest choice.

sec04-card-sec04-F44.front: What three changes linked to aging can make driving harder for older motorists?
sec04-card-sec04-F44.memory_hook: Duller senses, slower reactions, newer laws
sec04-card-sec04-F44.expected_back: Aging can dull hearing and eyesight, slow judgment and reaction in emergencies, and leave an older driver unaware of new rules and regulations.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: Why might an older motorist react less quickly during a sudden traffic emergency?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: Older drivers may not have the same ability to act quickly in an emergency as before, because physical dexterity may weaken with age.

sec04-card-sec04-F45.front: How many listed warning signs signal an older driver should adjust or stop driving, and who can assess skills?
sec04-card-sec04-F45.memory_hook: Two or three signs trigger review
sec04-card-sec04-F45.expected_back: If two or three of the listed warning signs apply to an older driver, it may be time to change driving habits or stop driving, and a doctor may refer the driver for an assessment by an SCDMV examiner or another trained medical professional.

sec04-card-sec04-F46.front: Which five parking, glare, object-recognition, and traffic-pacing troubles warn an older driver?
sec04-card-sec04-F46.memory_hook: Hard parking, glare, mistaking objects, lagging
sec04-card-sec04-F46.expected_back: Warning signs include needing several tries to parallel park, confusing objects such as a hydrant and a small child, long-lasting headlight glare discomfort, trouble keeping pace with traffic and slow starts at green lights.

sec04-card-sec04-F47.front: What four vehicle-damage, sign-reading, and close-up sight troubles add to the older-driver warning list?
sec04-card-sec04-F47.memory_hook: Fresh dents, missed signs, sudden confusion
sec04-card-sec04-F47.expected_back: More warning signs are frequent minor scrapes or dents, missing STOP and highway signs, confusion in unexpected situations and trouble making out objects a few feet away.

sec04-card-sec04-F48.front: Which two distance-judging and side-vision troubles also count as warning signs for older drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F48.memory_hook: Misjudging oncoming gaps, losing road edges
sec04-card-sec04-F48.expected_back: Trouble judging how far away an approaching vehicle is, or seeing the sides of the road while looking straight ahead, are also warning signs.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: Whom should you consult first about health concerns affecting driving, and what referral might follow?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.memory_hook: Consult your doctor for skill referral
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: For health concerns about driving the manual advises talking with a doctor, who may decide your driving skills should be assessed by an SCDMV examiner or a trained medical professional.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What two driving habits sum up South Carolina's reminder to give construction workers a brake?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: The manual asks drivers to give construction workers a brake: slow down in work zones and be ready to stop suddenly.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Which dangerous following habit does the South Carolina manual specifically ban inside work zones?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Do not tailgate other vehicles in a work zone.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: What dual penalties hit a South Carolina driver who endangers a highway worker?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: A driver who endangers a highway worker may be fined and have points added to their driving record, under SC Code §fifty-six-five-one thousand five hundred thirty-five.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: What shapes and background-plus-symbol colors identify regulatory traffic signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Regulatory signs are square, rectangular or a special shape, and they are white with black, red or green letters or symbols.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What legal force do regulatory signs carry, and which five driving rules do they commonly govern?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Regulatory signs state specific laws you must obey, covering matters such as traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed and parking.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What does a red circle with a diagonal red slash over a black symbol command?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: A regulatory sign showing a red circle with a red slash across a symbol prohibits the action pictured.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Contrast a standard white regulatory sign against one carrying a red circle and diagonal slash?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Regulatory signs in general state laws you must follow, while the version with a red circle and slash specifically forbids whatever action is pictured beneath it.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Which three banned-turn signs and three permitted-direction signs does South Carolina's regulatory section group together?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Common regulatory signs pictured include No U-Turn, No Left Turn, No Right Turn, Left Turn Only, Straight, and Straight or Turn Right.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What color scheme marks speed limit signs, and under what road conditions does that top speed apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Speed limit signs are black and white and give the maximum legal speed allowed in ideal conditions.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: What exact legal meaning does a black-and-white speed limit sign carry?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Speed limit signs are black-and-white signs showing the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: How many sides and which colors uniquely identify a stop sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: A stop sign is red with white letters and has eight sides.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Where must your front bumper come to rest at a stop sign with painted lines or walkways?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: At a stop sign you stop behind the stop line, or behind the crosswalk if there is one.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: When a stop sign has no painted stop line, what exact spot sets where you halt?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Where a stop sign has no stop line, stop at the point closest to the intersection from which you can see both ways without pulling into the cross traffic lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Once your wheels stop completely at a stop sign, what scan and priority duty come before moving?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: After stopping at a stop sign, look in all directions for crossing vehicles and pedestrians and yield the right-of-way.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: Compare the shape and letter colors of a stop sign with those of a yield sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: The stop sign is a red octagon with white letters, while the yield sign is a downward-pointing red and white triangle whose letters are red.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: How is a yield sign shaped and colored, and what driving action does it require?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: A yield sign is a red and white triangle pointing downward with red letters, and it means slow down and let traffic that has the right-of-way cross before you enter.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How does your braking duty at a stop sign differ from your duty at a yield sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A stop sign requires a stop and then yielding, whereas a yield sign requires slowing and letting right-of-way traffic cross before you enter.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Who may enter a Shared Center Lane Left Turn Only lane, and which two uses are illegal there?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.memory_hook: Left turns both ways; no passing
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: The Shared Center Lane Left Turn Only sign marks a lane reserved for vehicles turning left from either direction, and it is not for through traffic or for passing.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What rule do One-Way arrow signs enforce when turning onto or driving along a street?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: One-way street signs show that traffic moves only in the arrow's direction, so never turn against the arrow or drive the wrong way on a one-way street.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: Which two shapes and three background colors identify highway guide signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Guide signs are square or rectangular and colored green, brown or blue.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Pair the shapes and three colors of guide signs with the four kinds of travel help they give?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Guide signs are square or rectangular signs in green, brown, or blue that give intersecting-road information, directions to cities and towns, points of interest, and locations of hospitals, service stations, restaurants, and hotels.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Which four categories of navigation, sightseeing, and roadside-service help appear on guide signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Guide signs give information on intersecting roads, point you toward cities and towns, show points of interest and help you find hospitals, service stations, restaurants and hotels.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: What do the distinct shield shape and colors of a route number marker tell you?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: The shape and color of a route number sign show the type of road it marks: interstate, US, state, city, county or local.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: How should maps or GPS work together with roadside route shields on an unfamiliar trip?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Plan a trip with a road map or GPS device, then follow the route signs during the trip so you do not get lost in an unfamiliar area.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Which three primary route shields and one local marker make up South Carolina's route-sign family?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Route number signs pictured include Interstate Route, US Route and State Route signs, along with the Secondary System Road Marker.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: On a South Carolina Secondary System Road Marker starting with S, what do the first and last numbers identify?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: On a Secondary System Road Marker, the number right after the letter S tells you which county the road lies in, and the final number identifies the road itself.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How does South Carolina order county versus road numbers on an S marker, and do numbers repeat across counties?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: On the S road marker the county number comes first and the road number comes last, and each county keeps its own separate set of secondary road numbers.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: Are South Carolina's secondary road numbers unique statewide, or maintained separately per county?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Every county has its own separate set of secondary road numbers.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Which maps include every secondary road in a county, and how do you obtain them compared with the state primary map?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: All secondary roads appear on county maps, which can be bought by mail from the central office of the Department of Transportation, although the state primary system map shows only a few.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: What traffic do secondary system roads serve, and why should unfamiliar travelers skip rural ones?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Secondary system roads are local roads serving rural and urban traffic, and in rural areas they are not meant as through routes for drivers unfamiliar with the area.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Why does South Carolina advise drivers unfamiliar with a rural area against using secondary roads as shortcuts?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: In rural areas secondary system roads are not designed as through routes, which is why drivers who do not know the area should not normally use them.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: During a mandatory South Carolina coastal hurricane order, which blue route sign marks designated inland escape highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: If a hurricane strikes, a mandatory evacuation may be declared for South Carolina's coastal areas, and the Evacuation Route sign marks roads used for that kind of emergency.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: Which four painted elements on asphalt make up roadway pavement markings, and what two roles do they serve?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Pavement markings are lines, arrows, words or symbols painted on the road surface to give directions or warnings.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: Which five everyday lane, passing, turning, pedestrian, and stopping rules do pavement markings communicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Pavement markings divide lanes, show when you may pass or change lanes, show which lanes to use for turns, define pedestrian walkways and show where to stop for signs or signals.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: What traffic-direction arrangement do yellow centerline markings always signify?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: The yellow lane marking diagrams all show two-direction roadways.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Which three passing permissions can solid and dashed yellow centerlines create on a two-direction road?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: On two-direction roadways the diagrams show passing prohibited in both directions, passing permitted, and passing permitted only when the dashed line is on your side.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: When a two-way centerline pairs one solid yellow stripe with one dashed yellow stripe, which driver may pass?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: On a two-direction roadway, one yellow marking pattern allows passing only for the driver who has the dashed line on their side.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: What traffic direction and passing permission do broken white lane markings indicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: The white lane marking diagram shows a one-direction roadway on which passing is permitted.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: Beyond ordinary one-way and two-way lane stripes, which two specialized multi-lane controls does the manual highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Other lane controls pictured are the shared center left turn lane and reversible lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: How many common painted crosswalk styles does the South Carolina driver's manual highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: The manual pictures three common types of crosswalk markings.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What specific roadway zone does a crosswalk establish?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: A crosswalk defines the area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Walk through where to stop for a sign or signal with a stop line, a crosswalk, or neither?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: When a sign or signal makes you stop, stop behind the stop line or crosswalk, and if there is neither, stop at the nearest point where you can see both ways without entering cross traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Where neither a stop line nor a painted crosswalk exists, what determines your exact stopping point?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: With no stop line and no crosswalk, the stopping point is the spot nearest the intersection where you can see both ways without moving into cross traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: Must a pedestrian already be halfway across before you yield, or does stepping into a crosswalk count too?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.memory_hook: Yield to walkers inside or entering
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: You must yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk or entering one.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: How should you handle intersections that lack painted crosswalk lines when stopping or scanning?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: Not every crosswalk is marked, so watch for pedestrians at intersections, and if no crosswalk is apparent, stop before entering the intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: When a thick white stop line is painted ahead of a crosswalk, which marking governs your initial stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: Where a stop line comes before a crosswalk, the stop line must be obeyed first.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: If an approach has both an advance stop line and a painted crosswalk, why is rolling up to the crosswalk edge wrong?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: When a stop line and a crosswalk are both present and the stop line comes first, you stop at the stop line rather than at the crosswalk.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: What two physical traits make large commercial vehicles take much longer to stop than cars?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.memory_hook: Massive size and weight stretch stops
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Because of their size and weight, large vehicles take longer to stop than cars.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: At fifty-five miles per hour in ideal conditions, how far does a loaded truck need to stop, and how does that compare to a car?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.memory_hook: Three thirty-five feet; past one-half longer
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: A loaded truck with good tires and properly adjusted brakes, in ideal conditions at fifty-five miles per hour, needs at least three hundred thirty-five feet to stop, more than one and a half times a car's stopping distance.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Compare the hazard and distance of a truck's front no zone at fifty-five against its rear no zone?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.memory_hook: Front stops three-thirty-five; rear blinds two-hundred
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: The front no zone is about the truck's long stopping distance of at least three hundred thirty-five feet when loaded at fifty-five miles per hour, while the rear no zone is a blind spot reaching up to two hundred feet behind it.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Why must you never pull out onto a highway or whip into a lane directly ahead of a truck?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Because trucks stop so slowly, never pull onto a road or change lanes in front of a large vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: When passing a large truck, what mirror cue and speed habit govern merging back in front?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: When passing a large vehicle, wait until its whole front shows in your rearview mirror before moving in front of it, and keep up your speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: How far directly behind a large truck or bus can its rear blind spot extend?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Unlike cars, large vehicles have huge blind spots directly behind them that reach up to two hundred feet.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: What three dangers stack up at once when you tailgate right behind a large truck?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Following too close behind a large vehicle leaves you unseen by its driver, unable to see ahead, and with nowhere to go if it brakes suddenly.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: How should you position your car when following behind a large commercial vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Do not follow a large vehicle too closely, and position your vehicle so its driver can see you in the side mirrors.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Roughly how fast do large trucks travel on steep upgrades or downgrades, and which lane do they use?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: On steep hills, up or down, large vehicles must travel slowly, about thirty-five miles per hour, and so they use the right lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: At which two highway locations should passenger cars stay out of the right lane whenever possible?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Where possible, stay out of the right lane on hills and near truck weigh stations, where trucks try to re-enter faster traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Contrast why the right lane is risky on steep hills versus beside truck weigh stations?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Trucks crawl in the right lane on steep hills, while near weigh stations the right lane is where trucks merge back into faster traffic; both are reasons to stay out of that lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: What two habits keep you out of trouble whenever a large vehicle maneuvers?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Pay close attention to a large vehicle's turn signals and give it plenty of room to maneuver.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Why do trucks and buses sometimes swing wide to the left right before making a right turn?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: To turn right, a truck or bus driver may first swing wide to the left, sometimes using space from other lanes, to clear the curb corner.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Why must you never try to squeeze along the right curb beside a turning truck or bus?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Never try to slip between a turning truck or bus and the curb, where you could be squeezed into a serious collision; wait until it has finished its turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Where should you steer when meeting an oncoming truck on a two-lane road, and which way does wind push?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: When meeting a truck from the opposite direction, keep as far right as you can to avoid a sideswipe and to reduce the wind turbulence that pushes the two vehicles apart.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Why do many left-turn crashes involve oncoming trucks, and what is the rule when unsure?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Many large-vehicle collisions happen at intersections when drivers misjudge an approaching truck's speed before turning left, so if in doubt, do not turn left in its path.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: How does stopping behind painted intersection stop lines help large trucks and buses?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Stop lines set you farther back at an intersection so larger vehicles have more room to turn, so always stop behind them.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: Why shouldn't you dive in front of a truck to catch an exit or beat a single-lane work zone?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Never cut off a large vehicle, whether to make your exit or turn or to get ahead of a truck before a single-lane construction zone, because saving a few seconds is not worth a life.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Which three warning devices help emergency vehicles clear a path through traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Emergency vehicles carry sirens, flashing lights and special horns to help them move through traffic more efficiently.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: How do you yield to an approaching emergency vehicle running lights and siren, and what spots should stay unblocked?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.memory_hook: Pull to edge; keep junctions clear
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle has its flashing lights and siren on, yield by pulling over to the edge of the road so it can pass, and try not to block intersections, roads or driveways.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: Contrast how you yield to a moving emergency vehicle with siren on versus a stopped roadside responder?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.memory_hook: Pull over moving; shift lanes stopped
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: For a moving emergency vehicle with lights and siren on, you pull over to the road's edge, which differs from the lane change or slowdown used for a stopped one.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: Which roadside workers spurred South Carolina's move-over law, and what two actions does it require?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.memory_hook: Slow and shift for responders, tows
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Because more and more responders and tow truck operators are being struck on the road, South Carolina has a move-over law requiring drivers to slow down and change lanes when approaching emergency vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: When traffic and safety allow on a multi-lane road, how must you pass a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: When approaching a stopped authorized emergency vehicle, proceed with caution, slow down and yield by changing into a lane away from it if safety and traffic allow.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: What does South Carolina's move-over law require when heavy traffic makes changing lanes unsafe?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: If changing lanes away from a stopped emergency vehicle is unsafe, slow down and continue with caution at a speed that is safe for traffic conditions.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: What two law-enforcement reasons prompt an officer to initiate a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: An officer makes a traffic stop after seeing a traffic violation or while conducting a police investigation.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: What three immediate steps should you take when police lights flash behind your car?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: When you see emergency lights behind you, stay calm, turn on your signal and pull to the side of the road as soon as you safely can.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Once pulled over for an officer, what do you do with the engine, radio, hazards, and doors?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Once stopped, turn off the ignition and radio, switch on your hazard flashers and stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: What extra switch should you flip right after stopping for an officer at night?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: At night an officer may shine a spotlight on your vehicle, so switch on the interior lights right after stopping, which lets the officer see into the vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Where do your hands belong during a traffic stop, and what must passengers do?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Keep your hands on the steering wheel where they are easy to see, and have passengers stay calm, stay belted in the vehicle and keep their hands in plain view.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Why shouldn't anyone touch phones or rummage for papers before the officer speaks to you?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Neither you nor your passengers should use phones or other devices, and do not make sudden movements or dig for your license or papers before the officer gives instructions.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: When must you tell an officer about weapons inside the vehicle, and what applies to CWP holders?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: If there are any weapons in the vehicle, tell the officer about all of them at first contact, and concealed weapons permit holders should follow their CWP procedures.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: If stopped by someone in an unmarked vehicle or plain clothes, what may you politely request?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Roll down your window to talk with the officer, and if the officer is in an unmarked vehicle or not in uniform, ask to see law enforcement credentials.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: How should you handle an officer's request for license, registration, and insurance when they sit out of reach?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: The officer may ask for your driver's license, proof of insurance and vehicle registration, and if they are out of reach, say where they are and ask before reaching for them.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: If an officer directs you to exit your car, what two safety habits apply?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: If the officer asks you to step out, stay safely away from traffic and keep your hands in plain view.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: Where do you challenge a traffic ticket you believe is wrong, and what should you avoid roadside?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: The officer may issue a warning or a traffic ticket that may include a fine, and if you disagree, do not argue at the roadside, because you can explain your side in court.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: Does taking a traffic citation from an officer legally count as admitting guilt?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Accepting a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: How do accepting a ticket roadside and contesting the charge in court work together?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: Accepting a ticket does not mean you admit guilt, and contesting it happens in court rather than by arguing with the officer.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Compare South Carolina's rule on signing a traffic ticket with what can happen in other states?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: South Carolina does not require a driver to sign a traffic ticket, but in another state refusing to sign may lead to arrest under that state's laws.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Under what legal standard may an officer search your car without a court-issued warrant?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: If an officer believes a crime has been committed, the officer may search your vehicle without a court-issued warrant as long as there is probable cause.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What two safety and legal realities make fleeing law enforcement a disastrous mistake?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Never try to flee from law enforcement, since police chases cause many deadly collisions and the penalties for fleeing are worse than any original traffic citation.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: How and where should you report an officer who you believe acted improperly during a stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: If you believe an officer acted inappropriately, report it to the officer's agency promptly; the officer's name and agency appear on the ticket, or you may ask for them.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.front: What four emotional and physical boundaries must you keep even if you or passengers face arrest?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.expected_back: Do not make threatening motions or statements, keep your emotions in check, never interfere with the arrest of others with you and never resist arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: In what kind of driving environment must you stay extra alert for slow-moving vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Watch for slow-moving vehicles, especially in rural areas.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: What speed ceiling and vehicle types does a reflective orange-and-red rear triangle warn you about?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: A fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle on the back of a farm, construction or animal-drawn vehicle means it travels at less than twenty-five miles per hour, so approach with care and pass only when it is safe.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: Why shouldn't you assume a tractor or combine operator on a rural highway knows you are behind them?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Tractors, combines and other farm equipment cross roads and travel on rural state highways, and their operators most likely cannot hear approaching vehicles over the machinery noise, so pass with caution.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: What road rights and responsibilities apply to horseback riders and animal-drawn vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Animal-drawn vehicles and horseback riders have the same right to use the road as motor vehicles, must follow the same rules and can suffer heavy damage and injury if hit.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: What noises must you avoid near horses or buggies, and what sudden move should you anticipate?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: Pass animal-drawn vehicles and riders with caution, do not honk or rev your engine, which may scare the animal, and expect them to make left turns into fields and driveways.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.front: Contrast how noise affects passing a farm combine versus passing a horse-drawn wagon?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.expected_back: Farm machinery operators may not hear you coming, while animals pulling a vehicle or carrying a rider may be frightened by a horn or a revving engine.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: What three corner elements must you scan for before initiating a turn, and how do you alert others?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Before turning, search every corner for traffic controls, pedestrians and other vehicles, and signal what you intend to do.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Which lane must you move into and hold before making a turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Get into and stay in the lane nearest the direction you plan to turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Where should you aim your eyes while steering around a corner?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: During a turn, look through it to the farthest point you can see along your intended path.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Which wide steering habit must you avoid right before turning right?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: On a right turn, avoid swinging wide to the left before you turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: From which exact side of your lane should every right turn begin?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Always make a right turn from the right-most part of your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Whom must you yield to on a left turn, and from which side of your lane do you start?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and always turn from the left-most part of your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: Compare your starting position inside the lane for a right turn versus a left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Right turns start from the right-most part of your lane and left turns from the left-most part, so the side of the lane matches the direction of the turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: At intersections where two or more lanes turn together, what lane rule applies mid-turn?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Where more than one lane turns, pick and enter the lane you will turn from and stay in that same lane until the turn is finished.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: What three speed, blinker, and mirror steps complete a safe turn?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.memory_hook: Accelerate smoothly, cancel signal, check rear
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Once a turn is complete, speed up smoothly to a suitable speed, check that your turn signal has switched off and keep track of traffic behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What roadside openings does a two-point turnabout use, and when do you choose it?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: A two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse your direction when driving around a block is impractical or impossible.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: How do you signal, stop, check, and position your rear bumper to start a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: For a reverse two-point turnabout, signal right, stop and check traffic to the sides and rear, then back up until your rear bumper reaches the near edge of the driveway.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How do you work the steering wheel while backing slowly into the driveway during a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: While backing slowly into the driveway, steer quickly all the way to the right, then straighten the wheels and stop once the vehicle is centered in the driveway.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: What gear, traffic check, signal, and turn complete a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: The reverse two-point turnabout ends with a shift to drive, a check both ways and, if clear, a signal and a left turn into the proper lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: How do you set up and pull into an alley or driveway at the start of a forward two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: For a forward two-point turnabout, check your mirrors, signal left, ease toward the road's center, then pull into the alley or driveway keeping as far to its left side as you can.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: How far into the driveway do you pull on a forward two-point turnabout before shifting to reverse?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: In the forward two-point turnabout, stop when the rear of the vehicle clears the curb or driveway edge, check every direction, signal right and shift into reverse.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Walk through backing out and driving away at the end of a forward two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: The forward two-point turnabout ends by backing slowly while turning the wheel fully right, then straightening, stopping, shifting to drive, cancelling the right signal and moving forward once centered in the nearest lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Contrast a two-point turnabout against a three-point turn in whether driveways or side streets are used?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: A two-point turnabout relies on a driveway or alley, while a three-point turn must be done without using a side street or driveway at all.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: Under which three street-width, block, and traffic conditions is a three-point turnabout appropriate?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.memory_hook: Too narrow, no block, quiet two-lane
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Use a three-point turnabout only when the street is too narrow for a U-turn and you cannot go around the block, and only on a two-lane road that is not busy.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: What safer turnaround beats attempting a three-point turnabout on a busy city street?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: When the street is busy, circling an entire city block is better than attempting a three-point turnabout.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: Which three surface or boundary mistakes disqualify a clean three-point turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: A three-point turn must be done without hitting the curb, leaving the road surface or using a side street or driveway.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What mirror, signal, and curb-side stop open step one of a three-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Three-point step one: check the mirrors, turn on the right signal to show you are pulling to the right edge, and stop there.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: After stopping at the right edge, what signal, blind-spot check, and steering move make up step two?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.memory_hook: Left signal, shoulder check, hard left
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Three-point step two: signal left, check traffic and your left blind spot over your shoulder, then turn hard left across the road and stop when you reach the other side.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: During step three's backing leg, how must you check for traffic and which way do you turn the wheel?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Three-point step three: shift to reverse, check traffic and both blind spots over your shoulders instead of trusting the rearview mirror alone, then turn hard right back across and stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: How do you complete step four of a three-point turnabout and resume normal travel?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Three-point step four: shift to drive, check traffic and blind spots, turn hard left into the right lane of the new direction, make sure the signal has cancelled and drive straight on.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: As you near any intersection, what speed adjustment and five-part visual scan should kick in?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.memory_hook: Ease speed; scan controls, users, blind-spots
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Whenever you reach an intersection, reduce speed and scan for traffic controls, cross and oncoming traffic, people walking or cycling, the state of the road and spots where you cannot see well.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Why is counting on other drivers to obey stop signs or red lights a dangerous habit?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Do not depend on other road users to obey signals or signs, because you can control only your own driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: Even when priority rules favor you at a corner, what readiness keeps you out of crashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Some road users may not yield the right-of-way, so always be prepared to avoid a collision.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: After coming to a full stop at an intersection, what head-turn sequence spots cross traffic and bikes?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Once you have stopped at an intersection, give yourself extra time to spot crossing vehicles and bicyclists, and look left, then right, then left again before you enter.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: Why shouldn't you stomp the gas the instant a red light flips green?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: When a light turns green, do not move straight into the intersection; first make sure your path is clear and no traffic is crossing.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: How large a traffic gap must you wait for before crossing straight over or turning onto a road?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: You need a gap big enough to get all the way across the road, or to turn into the proper lane and build up to a suitable speed.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: When sizing up a tight lane or turn, should you expect other motorists to scoot over and share room?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Never assume another driver will share space with your vehicle or leave you any extra room.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: Why must you wait to see an approaching car actually turn rather than pulling out on its blinker alone?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Do not turn into a lane just because an approaching vehicle is signaling, since the driver may plan to turn after passing you or may have left the signal on from an earlier turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: How do directional crossovers inside a diverging diamond interchange simplify left turns onto ramps?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: A diverging diamond interchange, or DDI, differs from a conventional interchange in its directional crossovers on either side, which spare left-turning vehicles from crossing the path of oncoming through traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: Between the two signalized crossovers of a DDI, which side of the road carries cross-street traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: In a DDI, cross street traffic is shifted to the left side of the road between the signalized crossovers, so left turns onto or off the ramps do not conflict with traffic from other directions.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: How does a diverging diamond interchange compare with a conventional diamond on ramp turns and conflict points?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: The DDI design has improved turning movements to and from the interstate and sharply cut vehicle-to-vehicle conflict points compared with a conventional diamond interchange.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: Along with reducing total conflict points, how does a DDI change the crashes that could still occur?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Besides cutting the number of conflicts, the DDI also lowers how severe those conflicts are.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: Which two high-risk maneuvers does a restricted crossing U-turn intersection eliminate from side-street approaches?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: A restricted crossing U-turn, or RCUT, intersection removes left-turn and through movements from the cross street approaches.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: How does a cross-street driver go left or straight across a divided highway at an RCUT?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: At an RCUT, drivers coming from the cross street turn right onto the main road and then make a U-turn at a one-way median opening.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: Which four types of traffic control devices can manage movements through an RCUT intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: An RCUT turns a cross street left or through movement into a right turn followed by a U-turn at a median opening, and it can be controlled by a signal, a stop sign, or a merge or yield sign.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: What overall safety result do RCUT intersections deliver on multi-lane corridors?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: RCUT intersections reduce potential conflict points and increase safety.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: Around the center island of a roundabout or traffic circle, which direction does traffic circulate and who yields?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: A roundabout, also known as a traffic circle, is a circular intersection where vehicles travel counterclockwise around a raised center island and entering traffic yields to circulating traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: How should you adjust speed when nearing a roundabout or traffic circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Slow down as you enter a roundabout or traffic circle, which a warning sign may announce ahead of time.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Walk through the four steps from reaching a roundabout yield line to taking your exit?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Yield to the traffic already in the roundabout, enter in a counterclockwise direction, then go to your exit, signal and leave.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: Between a driver waiting at a roundabout entrance and a driver already circling inside, who holds priority?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: At a roundabout the entering driver is the one who yields, and the vehicles already circulating keep the right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: Eliminating which two deadly crash types makes roundabouts safer than traditional four-way intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Roundabouts are safer than traditional intersections because they remove head-on and high-speed right-angle collisions.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: Which flashing light colors or side equipment on a stopped or stopping school bus command you to stay stopped?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: For as long as a school bus is stopped or getting ready to stop with red or amber lights flashing or its stop arm out, you must remain stopped.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: In South Carolina, may you hurry past a slowing school bus whose amber lights are flashing before red starts?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: Either red or amber flashing lights on a stopped or stopping school bus, or its extended stop arm, mean you must stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: Once school bus lights go dark and the stop arm retracts out of sight, how should you proceed?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: After the school bus lights stop flashing and the stop arm can no longer be seen, move on slowly and watch for children.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: On a two-lane South Carolina road, which directions of traffic must stop for a stopped school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: On a two-lane road you are required to stop for a stopped school bus, whether you are meeting it or following it.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: On a four-lane or wider multi-lane South Carolina highway, which direction must stop for a school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: On a four-lane or other multi-lane highway, the school bus stopping rule applies only when you are traveling behind the bus.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: Contrast oncoming drivers' school-bus duty on a two-lane road against a four-lane or multi-lane highway in South Carolina?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: On a multi-lane highway a driver meeting a school bus from the other direction is not covered by the stopping rule, while on a two-lane road every driver must stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: What must you do if a school bus ahead activates red or amber flashing lights just as you try to overtake it?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: You must also stop when you are trying to pass a school bus whose red or amber signals are flashing.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: Under what dual condition may traffic pass a stopped school bus without stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: You need not stop when the school bus sits in a passenger loading zone entirely off the main travel lanes and pedestrians are not permitted to cross the road.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which everyday vehicles fall under a South Carolina Class D license, and what gross weight ceiling applies?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: A Class D license covers non-commercial passenger vehicles, such as cars and trucks, that weigh no more than twenty-six thousand pounds GVW.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Which vehicle weight figure decides the South Carolina license class needed, and where does Class D top out?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: Class D covers non-commercial passenger vehicles such as cars and trucks that do not exceed twenty-six thousand pounds gross vehicle weight, and gross vehicle weight rating or gross vehicle weight determines the license class needed.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: Which South Carolina license class covers heavy non-commercial single-unit vehicles like large motor homes?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Class E covers non-commercial single-unit vehicles above twenty-six thousand pounds GVW, such as big trucks and motor homes.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which license class covers non-commercial vehicle combinations topping twenty-six thousand pounds, like a motor home towing a car?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Class F covers non-commercial combination vehicles above twenty-six thousand pounds GVW, such as a truck or motor home pulling a trailer or another vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How do South Carolina's Class E and Class F licenses split non-commercial vehicles above twenty-six thousand pounds?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.memory_hook: Single unit E, hitched combo F
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: Class E is for a single non-commercial vehicle over twenty-six thousand pounds GVW, while Class F is for a non-commercial combination over twenty-six thousand pounds GVW, such as a motor home towing a trailer.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Which smaller rides may Class D, E, and F drivers operate automatically, and which sidecar setup stays off-limits?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Class E and Class F holders, like Class D holders, may also operate a moped or a three-wheel vehicle, but not a two-wheel motorcycle with a detachable sidecar.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What minimum age and testing steps apply when getting South Carolina's Class G moped license?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Class G is the moped license: the minimum age is fifteen and only the vision and knowledge tests are required.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Does someone holding a valid license or permit in one of the other four classes need Class G to ride a moped?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: A driver who already holds a valid license or permit in any of the other four classes needs no separate license to ride a moped.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Which two-wheel and three-wheel machines fall under South Carolina's Class M license?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Class M covers two-wheel motorcycles, with or without a detachable sidecar, and three-wheel vehicles.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Contrast how another valid license class treats riding a moped versus riding a two-wheel motorcycle?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: A moped needs no separate license for a holder of any other valid license or permit, while a two-wheel motorcycle always needs Class M.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How is someone licensed if they drive both a car and a motorcycle, and what testing earns it?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.memory_hook: One card endorsed after both tests
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Someone who drives both a motorcycle and another type of vehicle gets one license endorsed for two classifications after passing driving tests for both.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What combined weight rating and towed-unit rating trigger a Class A commercial driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: A Class A CDL covers vehicle combinations with a GCWR of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more when the towed unit's GVWR is over ten thousand pounds.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Which heavy single vehicles—and what light-trailer limit—fall under a Class B commercial license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: A Class B CDL covers a single vehicle with a GVWR of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, including one towing no more than ten thousand pounds GVWR.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which two passenger-count or cargo-placard uses place a smaller commercial vehicle into Class C?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: A Class C CDL covers vehicles that fit neither Class A nor B but are designed to carry sixteen or more people counting the driver, or are placarded for hazardous materials.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: Why is Class C unique among the three commercial license classes?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.memory_hook: Defined by cargo, passengers, not weight
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: A Class C CDL is defined by use, not weight: vehicles built for sixteen or more occupants including the driver, or placarded for hazardous materials, when they are not Class A or B.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: How many valid driver's licenses may one qualified person hold at once?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Each qualified driver holds just one license endorsed for one or more classes, and having more than one valid license is illegal.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which three documents matching your vehicle class must be with you whenever you drive or risk a fine?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Behind the wheel you must have a valid license, the vehicle registration and a valid insurance card for that class of vehicle, or you can be fined.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Which five facts must a U.S. citizen prove with original documents under Form MV-93 for a first SC card?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: A US citizen applying for a first permit, license or ID card brings originals that prove US citizenship, identity, birth date and birthplace, Social Security number and South Carolina address, as listed on form MV-ninety-three.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Where does a non-U.S. citizen apply for a South Carolina credential, and which checklist form governs?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: An applicant who is not a US citizen applies at a branch that processes international customers, following the checklist on form MV-ninety-four.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Who must begin with a South Carolina beginner's permit, and what age and tests unlock it?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Anyone who has never held a driver's license starts with a beginner's permit, which requires an age of at least fifteen and passing the vision and knowledge tests.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Between six in the morning and midnight, who must sit beside a beginner's permit driver?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: On a beginner's permit you may drive from six a.m. to midnight with a licensed driver in the front seat who is at least twenty-one and has at least one year of experience.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: How do supervision rules tighten if a beginner's permit holder drives past midnight?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Permit driving after midnight needs supervision by a licensed person from the list in SC Code §fifty-six-one-one hundred(A)(one-seven).

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Compare who may supervise a beginner's permit from six in the morning to midnight versus after midnight?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: Beginner's permit supervision by day needs a licensed driver aged at least twenty-one with one year of experience, while after midnight it must be a licensed person from the statute's list.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: Counting from the day you get your beginner's permit, what is the earliest day you can apply for a license?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: The earliest you may apply for any license after getting a beginner's permit is the one hundred eighty-first day, and any day after that also works.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: How many total and nighttime practice hours must a fifteen- or sixteen-year-old permit holder log with an approved supervisor?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A permit holder who is fifteen or sixteen must practice at least forty hours, with ten of those hours at night, beside an approved supervisor such as a father, mother or legal guardian.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: What notarized permission and filing step let another responsible adult serve as item seven on the teen supervisor list?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Item seven on the approved teen practice supervisor list is a responsible adult willing to assume the duties under South Carolina Code fifty-six dash one dash one hundred ten who holds notarized written permission from someone in items one through six and provides SCDMV with a copy.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: What two written steps let someone approved by the Department of Social Services supervise teen driving practice?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: A person approved in writing by the Department of Social Services may supervise teen practice, and the SCDMV must receive a copy of that approval.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: How long must a first-time applicant aged seventeen or older hold a beginner's permit before skills testing for full privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: A first-time applicant aged seventeen or older must have held a beginner's permit for more than one hundred eighty days before taking the skills test for full privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Beyond holding a permit past one hundred eighty days, which three extra requirements apply to fifteen- and sixteen-year-old applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.memory_hook: Driver ed, school standing, logged hours
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: A first-time applicant who is fifteen or sixteen needs more than one hundred eighty days on the permit plus completed driver education, school enrollment with satisfactory attendance and the logged practice hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: How many classroom hours and behind-the-wheel driving hours make up South Carolina's required teen driver's education?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: A first-time applicant aged fifteen or sixteen must have completed driver's education with eight hours in the classroom and six hours of driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Which three school-status requirements must a fifteen- or sixteen-year-old meet to get licensed?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: That teen applicant must also be enrolled in school, not suspended or expelled, and have satisfactory attendance.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What three things does Form PDLA certify for teens, and who issues the form?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Teens submit form PDLA, the Certification of School Attendance, Driver's Education and Driving Practice, which the driver's education program hands out after the course is passed.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: Which teen ages fall under South Carolina's graduated driver's license program, and how is it structured?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: The graduated driver's license program serves ages fifteen to seventeen and limits night and unsupervised driving at first, easing those limits over time.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: What narrow age bracket and two exams qualify a teen for a conditional license?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A conditional license is open to applicants at least fifteen and a half but under sixteen who pass the vision and skills tests.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: When may a conditional licensee drive solo in standard versus daylight saving time, and when must an adult ride along?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.memory_hook: Solo six-to-six or eight, adult midnight
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: A conditional licensee may drive alone from six a.m. to six p.m., or until eight p.m. during daylight saving time, and with a licensed driver aged twenty-one or older from then until midnight.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: How does daylight saving time shift the evening cutoff for solo driving on a conditional license?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Solo driving on a conditional license ends at six p.m. in standard time but at eight p.m. during daylight saving time.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: How many under-twenty-one passengers may conditional or special restricted drivers carry solo, and what three exceptions apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Conditional and special restricted licensees may carry at most two passengers under twenty-one unless a licensed adult aged twenty-one or older rides along, except when carrying family members or students to and from school.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: What one-year record earns a conditional licensee full driving privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.memory_hook: One year clean, zero at-fault wrecks
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: A conditional licensee earns full privileges after holding the license for one year with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collisions.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Who must supervise conditional or special restricted drivers if they drive between midnight and six in the morning?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.memory_hook: Midnight to six needs statute-listed adult
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: From midnight to six a.m., conditional and special restricted licensees may drive only when supervised by a licensed person from the list in SC Code §fifty-six-one-one hundred(A)(one-seven).

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: What suspension hits a driver under seventeen who racks up six or more points within the first license year?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: A driver under seventeen who collects six or more points before holding the license for one year has it suspended for six months.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: Which two paths qualify a sixteen-year-old under seventeen for a special restricted license?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.memory_hook: Pass tests sixteen, or hold conditional
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: The special restricted license is for applicants who are sixteen but under seventeen and pass the vision and skills tests, or who are sixteen and already hold a conditional license.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does holding a conditional license connect once a driver turns sixteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: A sixteen-year-old who already holds a conditional license qualifies for the special restricted license, so the two teen stages follow one another.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: How late does an approved waiver let a sixteen-year-old drive solo for work or extracurriculars, and what stays off-limits?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: A sixteen-year-old with a special restricted or conditional license may get a waiver to drive alone until midnight for work or certain extracurricular activities, but never after midnight.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Can a sixteen-year-old's evening waiver ever authorize driving solo at twelve-thirty in the morning?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: A waiver extends a sixteen-year-old's solo driving to midnight for work or certain activities, yet driving after midnight is still not allowed under it.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: Which forms, letters, screening, and fee are required at an SCDMV branch to get an evening waiver?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.memory_hook: Two forms, two letters, vision, twenty-five
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: The waiver needs a branch visit with form four hundred forty-seven-NC, the Consent for Minor form four hundred forty-seven-CM signed by a qualified adult before SCDMV staff, two letters, a vision test and a twenty-five dollars fee.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: Who writes each of the two explanatory letters required for a sixteen-year-old's driving waiver?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: For the waiver you bring a letter from the school, church, work or activity explaining the need, and a letter from a parent or legal guardian approving it and explaining why.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: What two milestones grant a teen full driving privileges without even visiting an SCDMV branch?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.memory_hook: Turn seventeen or one clean year
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: Full privileges arrive at seventeen, or after a year on a conditional or special restricted license with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collisions, with no branch visit needed.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: Compare the record-based route and the birthday route to full teen driving privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: Full privileges come with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collisions during the year on a teen license, otherwise turning seventeen is the other route.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: What item does SCDMV mail when you earn full teen privileges, and how must you use it?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Once you reach full privileges the SCDMV mails you a sleeve, and you must keep the license inside it to use those full privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: Which three tests apply to an original license or class upgrade, and where can vision and knowledge be taken?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: An original license or an upgrade to a different class requires vision, knowledge and skills tests, and the vision and knowledge tests can be taken at any SCDMV branch.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: Which single first-time license skips the behind-the-wheel skills test that every other class requires?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: Every first license test includes vision, knowledge and skills tests except the moped license, which needs no skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: Contrast the test lineup for a first moped license against every other original South Carolina license?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: A moped license needs vision and knowledge tests only, while every other first license also needs a skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: Who owes a road exam, and which two interchangeable names does the South Carolina manual use for it?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: A skills test is required for anyone who does not hold a valid driver's license, and the manual uses the names skills test and driving test for the same exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F46.front: Which three subject areas appear on the knowledge exam, and what should glasses or contact wearers bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F46.expected_back: The knowledge test covers traffic laws, road signs and driving safety rules, and corrective lenses should be brought or worn for the vision test.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: Which three testing-room violations cause an automatic failure on the knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.memory_hook: Leaving, talking, or bringing devices, notes
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: You fail the knowledge test if you leave the test area before finishing, talk to anyone, or bring in written material or any electronic device such as a phone, laptop or tablet.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: Which exams and license classes may third-party One Stop Driver Training and Testing Programs administer?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.memory_hook: Class D first-timers and Class M
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: One Stop Driver Training and Testing Programs, also called third-party testers, may give the knowledge and or or skills tests for a first-time Class D permit or license and a Class M license.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: Even after passing with a third-party tester, what can SCDMV randomly require before issuing your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: The SCDMV may randomly select an applicant to pass the skills test again before the license is issued, under SC Code §fifty-six-one-fifteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: What is the examiner checking while riding beside you, and will they try to trick you into errors?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: The examiner rides along only to confirm you can control the vehicle and obey the rules of the road, and will not try to trick you.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: Who supplies the skills-test car, and which five safety items appear on the first inspection list?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.memory_hook: Supply car; lights, brakes, wipers, mirrors
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: You must provide the skills test vehicle, and it must be safe with working headlights, brakes, windshield wipers, mirrors and speedometer.

sec01-card-sec01-F42.front: Which four additional cabin controls and three vehicle credentials must your skills-test car also have?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.expected_back: The test vehicle also needs working safety belts, turn signals, defroster and horn, plus a valid license plate, registration card and insurance card.

sec01-card-sec01-F43.front: What happens if your test car is unsafe versus if you forget to fasten your seat belt during the skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F43.expected_back: An unsafe vehicle gets the skills test postponed, and not wearing your seat belt during the test is an automatic fail.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.front: Distinguish the exact outcome of bringing an unsafe vehicle from driving unbuckled on skills-test day?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.expected_back: An unsafe test vehicle means the test is postponed, whereas skipping your seat belt means an automatic fail.

sec01-card-sec01-F44.front: Which three items or people must accompany you when checking in for the skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F44.memory_hook: Prior card, licensed driver, SC insurance
sec01-card-sec01-F44.expected_back: Bring your old license or permit if you have one, a licensed driver, and liability insurance information from a company licensed to do business in SC.

sec01-card-sec01-F45.front: Who is allowed inside or standing around the vehicle once the skills test begins?
sec01-card-sec01-F45.expected_back: Only you and the SCDMV employee who tests you may be in or around the vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F47.front: Along with controls, turns, signs, parallel and hill parking, how far do you back straight and what turnabout appears?
sec01-card-sec01-F47.expected_back: Skills test tasks may include working the lights, wipers, signals and four-way flashers, a brake light check, lane changes and turns, naming signs, parallel parking, one hundred feet of straight backing, hill parking and a reverse two-point turnabout.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Because starting procedures vary across vehicles, where should you check how to start yours?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Because vehicles differ, look in your owner's manual to learn how to start the one you are driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What three steps with your right foot, gear selector, and ignition start the engine safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: To start the engine, put your right foot on the brake pedal, confirm the gear selector is in park, then turn the key to the on position or push and release the start button.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: Which gear position belongs to starting the engine, and when do you shift into drive?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The gear selector should be in park when you start the engine, and you move it to D for drive only when you are ready to pull away.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Right after the engine starts running, which four types of dashboard warnings or gauges need a scan?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Once the engine runs, look over the gauges and any dashboard indicator lights that need attention, such as fuel, oil, ABS or air bag warnings.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What gear move and forward check come first when you prepare to pull away?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: To pull away, move the gear selector to D for drive and make sure the path ahead of the vehicle is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: Along with looking ahead, which three zones around the vehicle require checks before moving?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Before moving, also check the sides, the rear and your blind spots, looking over your shoulder for any traffic or obstacles.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: What communication step comes right before moving your foot onto the accelerator to pull out?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Give a signal and, if it is safe, move your foot to the accelerator and press it gently.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: How should your foot and heel press the accelerator to build speed smoothly?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Build speed slowly and evenly, pressing the pedal with the top of your foot while your heel rests on the floor.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: What must you check before moving your foot from the gas pedal to the brake?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: To stop, first check your mirrors for traffic behind you, then shift your foot from the accelerator to the brake pedal.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: When slowing to a stop, which happens first between checking mirrors and moving your foot to brake?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Stopping begins with a mirror check for traffic behind you, and only then does your foot move from the accelerator to the brake.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: What kind of foot pressure should stay on the brake pedal until the wheels stop turning?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Keep steady pressure on the brake pedal until the vehicle has stopped.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Whether rolling forward or backing in reverse, which way do you turn the steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: You turn the steering wheel toward the direction you want the vehicle to go, whether you are moving forward or in reverse.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Where on the steering wheel should both hands rest, and how tight should your grip feel?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Hold the outside of the steering wheel with both hands on opposite sides, using a grip that is firm but gentle.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: How should your fingers and thumbs hold the wheel, and which grip is strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Grip the wheel with your fingers rather than your palms, keep your thumbs up along its face, and never turn it while holding the inside of the rim.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Using a clock face, which hour ranges mark proper placement for your left and right hands?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Picturing the wheel as a clock face, your left hand belongs in the seven to nine o'clock area and your right hand in the three to five o'clock area.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: When is taking one hand briefly off the steering wheel acceptable while driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Both hands stay on the wheel at all times except when one is needed for another driving task, such as shifting gears, switching on the wipers or giving hand signals.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Which three driver hand signals justify taking one hand off the steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: The hand signals that may take one hand off the wheel are those for turning, slowing or stopping.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: What type of roadway should a new driver choose first when learning basic vehicle handling?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: When you first learn to handle a car or truck, pick lightly traveled rural roads if you can.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: What steering milestone shows you are ready to move on to practicing turns and parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: When you can steer accurately and keep making the small corrections steering always needs, you are ready to practice skills such as turning and parking.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How does holding the wheel in the lower seven-to-nine and three-to-five zones improve lane keeping?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Keeping the hands in the seven to nine and three to five o'clock areas tends to reduce muscle strain, which means less steering that causes weaving within a lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: At what speeds and in what maneuvers should you use hand-over-hand steering?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Hand-over-hand steering is for turning the wheel at low speeds, for example at an intersection or while parking.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Where on the steering-wheel clock face do your left and right hands begin hand-over-hand steering?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: For hand-over-hand steering, start with your left hand between eight and nine o'clock and your right hand between three and four o'clock.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Which sections of the wheel rim execute right and left hand-over-hand turns, and how do you straighten?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: In hand-over-hand steering you use the right top third of the wheel to turn right and the left top third to turn left, repeating as needed, then reverse the process to straighten out.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: In what two narrow situations does the manual allow steering with a single hand?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: One-hand steering is only for backing up or for a short reach to controls such as the wipers, flashers or lights.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: While one hand reaches briefly for wipers or lights, where must your steering hand stay?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: When you must reach for a control, keep your other hand at the normal operating position of eight to nine or three to four o'clock, depending on how the wheel is designed.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Which steering method shares the exact eight-to-nine and three-to-four clock zones used during a one-hand reach?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: While one hand reaches for a control, the hand that stays on the wheel keeps the normal operating position of eight to nine or three to four o'clock, the same areas where hand-over-hand steering starts.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What three safety reasons explain why at least one hand must stay on the wheel at all times?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.memory_hook: Keep balance, handle reversals, prevent injury
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Keeping one hand on the wheel at all times matters for vehicle balance, for handling steering reversals and for avoiding injury.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: When is placing a hand at twelve o'clock on the steering wheel recommended?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: A twelve o'clock hand position is recommended only when you back up to the left or right and must turn in your seat to see the path behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: In the manual's backing-up steps, which hand takes the twelve o'clock spot on the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Backing up is the only situation in which the manual recommends the twelve o'clock position, and its backing steps put the left hand there.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: What check must happen before climbing into the driver's seat to back out, and why?
