sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Even from the back or covered in frost, an eight-sided octagon silhouette belongs exclusively to a stop sign.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Where must your front bumper come to rest at a stop sign with painted lines or walkways?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Halting behind the painted bar or crosswalk keeps pedestrians from having to step into cross traffic around your hood.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: When a stop sign has no painted stop line, what exact spot sets where you halt?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Stopping closest to the corner with two-way sightlines, without nosing into cross lanes, keeps you safe and informed.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Once your wheels stop completely at a stop sign, what scan and priority duty come before moving?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Treating a quick pause as an automatic ticket forward ignores crossing pedestrians and priority vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Compare the shape and letter colors of a stop sign with those of a yield sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Stop signs print white letters on an eight-sided red face, while yield signs print red letters inside a downward triangle.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How is a yield sign shaped and colored, and what driving action does it require?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Easing speed early at a downward red-and-white triangle lets you blend smoothly or stop if cross traffic holds priority.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How does your braking duty at a stop sign differ from your duty at a yield sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Stop signs demand zero wheel roll every single time, whereas yield signs allow rolling slowly when cross paths are empty.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Who may enter a Shared Center Lane Left Turn Only lane, and which two uses are illegal there?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Cruising straight or overtaking inside a two-way center turn lane risks head-on crashes with opposing left-turners.
sec08-card-sec08-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Left turns both ways; no passing

visual_sync.text_span: Left turns both ways; no passing

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What rule do One-Way arrow signs enforce when turning onto or driving along a street?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Turning against a black-and-white One-Way arrow puts your bumper nose-to-nose with every lane of oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Which two shapes and three background colors identify highway guide signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Green routes destinations, brown highlights parks and historic sites, and blue points out motorist services.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Pair the shapes and three colors of guide signs with the four kinds of travel help they give?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Connecting green, brown, and blue rectangles to junctions, towns, attractions, and food-lodging-hospitals covers every guide question.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Which four categories of navigation, sightseeing, and roadside-service help appear on guide signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Reading guide boards ahead lets you move into exit lanes calmly for towns, parks, hospitals, fuel, or lodging.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: What do the distinct shield shape and colors of a route number marker tell you?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Telling red-and-blue Interstate shields apart from US, state, or county shields keeps your highway navigation accurate.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: How should maps or GPS work together with roadside route shields on an unfamiliar trip?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Mapping your route parked and matching shields along the drive prevents sudden last-second swerves across exits.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Which three primary route shields and one local marker make up South Carolina's route-sign family?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: South Carolina pairs standard Interstate, US, and State shields with its own S-coded Secondary System Road Marker.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: On a South Carolina Secondary System Road Marker starting with S, what do the first and last numbers identify?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: South Carolina's S-number code puts the county identifier right after S and the specific local road number last.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How does South Carolina order county versus road numbers on an S marker, and do numbers repeat across counties?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Because every county runs its own secondary list, the county code after S keeps duplicate road numbers distinct.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: Are South Carolina's secondary road numbers unique statewide, or maintained separately per county?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Road fifty in one county is completely unrelated to road fifty across the next county line.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Which maps include every secondary road in a county, and how do you obtain them compared with the state primary map?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Statewide primary maps omit most local S-roads, whereas DOT county maps bought by mail plot every single one.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: What traffic do secondary system roads serve, and why should unfamiliar travelers skip rural ones?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Rural secondary roads serve local farms and neighborhoods rather than long-distance through travel.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Why does South Carolina advise drivers unfamiliar with a rural area against using secondary roads as shortcuts?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Winding local S-roads lack through-highway design and signage, making them easy places for outsiders to get turned around.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: During a mandatory South Carolina coastal hurricane order, which blue route sign marks designated inland escape highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Following blue Evacuation Route shields keeps coastal traffic channeled onto managed high-capacity corridors.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: Which four painted elements on asphalt make up roadway pavement markings, and what two roles do they serve?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Painted surface cues reinforce overhead signs right inside your forward line of sight.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: Which five everyday lane, passing, turning, pedestrian, and stopping rules do pavement markings communicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Reading lane stripes, turn arrows, crosswalk bars, and stop lines keeps your car positioned legally without guessing.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: What traffic-direction arrangement do yellow centerline markings always signify?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Seeing yellow paint on your left warns immediately that the lane beyond carries oncoming vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Which three passing permissions can solid and dashed yellow centerlines create on a two-direction road?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Double solid yellow locks both ways, broken yellow opens both, and mixed lines grant passing strictly to the dashed side.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: When a two-way centerline pairs one solid yellow stripe with one dashed yellow stripe, which driver may pass?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Sightlines open for one direction before the other on hills and curves, so only the broken-line side gets passing rights.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What traffic direction and passing permission do broken white lane markings indicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: White dashes divide lanes moving the same way and permit safe lane changes and overtaking.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Beyond ordinary one-way and two-way lane stripes, which two specialized multi-lane controls does the manual highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Recognizing center two-way left-turn markings and overhead-controlled reversible lanes prevents wrong-way lane entries.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: How many common painted crosswalk styles does the South Carolina driver's manual highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Whether striped with parallel bars, ladder blocks, or diagonal hatches, all three styles reserve pedestrian crossing space.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What specific roadway zone does a crosswalk establish?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Channeling foot traffic into defined crossing zones tells motorists exactly where to keep bumpers clear and yield.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: Walk through where to stop for a sign or signal with a stop line, a crosswalk, or neither?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Obeying painted lines or walkways first, and using the nearest safe two-way sight point when unmarked, protects every user.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Where neither a stop line nor a painted crosswalk exists, what determines your exact stopping point?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Pulling to the nearest point with left-and-right visibility while staying short of cross traffic balances sight and safety.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Must a pedestrian already be halfway across before you yield, or does stepping into a crosswalk count too?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Waiting until someone reaches your exact lane cuts it too close; yield as soon as they are in or entering.
sec08-card-sec08-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Yield to walkers inside or entering

visual_sync.text_span: Yield to walkers inside or entering

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: How should you handle intersections that lack painted crosswalk lines when stopping or scanning?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Pedestrians cross legally at unpainted corners too, so halt short of the intersection box and scan both curbs.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: When a thick white stop line is painted ahead of a crosswalk, which marking governs your initial stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Stopping back at the advance white bar keeps sightlines open and buffers the pedestrian walkway.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: If an approach has both an advance stop line and a painted crosswalk, why is rolling up to the crosswalk edge wrong?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Passing the stop line to wait at the crosswalk edge violates the advance stop bar placed for turning trucks and walkers.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: What two physical traits make large commercial vehicles take much longer to stop than cars?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Momentum scales with mass, so even top-condition air brakes cannot stop forty tons like a sedan.
sec14-card-sec14-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Massive size and weight stretch stops

visual_sync.text_span: Massive size and weight stretch stops

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour in ideal conditions, how far does a loaded truck need to stop, and how does that compare to a car?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: More than a football field of pavement disappears before a highway semi halts, over one-and-a-half car stops.
sec14-card-sec14-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Three thirty-five feet; past one-half longer

visual_sync.text_span: Three thirty-five feet; past one-half longer

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: Compare the hazard and distance of a truck's front no zone at fifty-five against its rear no zone?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Cutting in front steals three hundred thirty-five stopping feet, while tailgating hides inside two hundred blind feet.
sec14-card-sec14-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Front stops three-thirty-five; rear blinds two-hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Front stops three-thirty-five; rear blinds two-hundred

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Why must you never pull out onto a highway or whip into a lane directly ahead of a truck?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Stealing a truck's front cushion leaves the driver physically unable to brake short of your rear bumper.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: When passing a large truck, what mirror cue and speed habit govern merging back in front?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Wait until the entire front of the cab fills your inside mirror and stay on the gas.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: How far directly behind a large truck or bus can its rear blind spot extend?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Box trailers have no center rearview mirror, creating a blind tunnel up to two hundred feet long.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: What three dangers stack up at once when you tailgate right behind a large truck?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Riding a trailer bumper blinds both the trucker to you and you to hazards ahead when air brakes lock.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: How should you position your car when following behind a large commercial vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Dropping back until you spot the rig's side mirrors ensures the driver knows you are back there.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Roughly how fast do large trucks travel on steep upgrades or downgrades, and which lane do they use?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Heavy rigs keep right around thirty-five miles per hour both climbing steep grades and holding gears downhill.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: At which two highway locations should passenger cars stay out of the right lane whenever possible?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Moving left early avoids slow rigs on grades and merging semis accelerating out of weigh stations.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Contrast why the right lane is risky on steep hills versus beside truck weigh stations?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Grades slow rigs to a crawl while scale ramps feed heavy accelerating trucks back into highway flow.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: What two habits keep you out of trouble whenever a large vehicle maneuvers?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Spotting a trailer blinker early lets you hang back and leave generous multi-lane turning clearance.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Why do trucks and buses sometimes swing wide to the left right before making a right turn?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Rear trailer wheels track tighter than front cab wheels and would mount the sidewalk without swinging wide.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: Why must you never try to squeeze along the right curb beside a turning truck or bus?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: That tempting open gap on the right closes like scissors as the trailer swings around the corner.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Where should you steer when meeting an oncoming truck on a two-lane road, and which way does wind push?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Hugging the right edge prevents sideswipes and softens the air blast that shoves passing vehicles apart.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Why do many left-turn crashes involve oncoming trucks, and what is the rule when unsure?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Large vehicles appear to move slower than their true speed, so any doubt means waiting to turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: How does stopping behind painted intersection stop lines help large trucks and buses?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Creeping past the white bar blocks the nose sweep a fifty-foot trailer needs to turn cleanly.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: Why shouldn't you dive in front of a truck to catch an exit or beat a single-lane work zone?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Cutting across a heavy bumper before cones or exit ramps trades a few seconds for fatal crash risk.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: Which three warning devices help emergency vehicles clear a path through traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Hearing a siren or air horn before spotting strobes warns you to scan mirrors and clear space.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: How do you yield to an approaching emergency vehicle running lights and siren, and what spots should stay unblocked?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Pulling to the curb without blocking intersections, side roads, or driveways keeps the responder's turn path open.
sec14-card-sec14-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Pull to edge; keep junctions clear

visual_sync.text_span: Pull to edge; keep junctions clear

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: Contrast how you yield to a moving emergency vehicle with siren on versus a stopped roadside responder?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Approaching sirens send you to the road edge, whereas parked flashing lights call for a lane change or slowdown.
sec14-card-sec14-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Pull over moving; shift lanes stopped

visual_sync.text_span: Pull over moving; shift lanes stopped

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: Which roadside workers spurred South Carolina's move-over law, and what two actions does it require?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Rising roadside strikes on emergency crews and tow operators led South Carolina to mandate slowing and changing lanes.
sec14-card-sec14-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Slow and shift for responders, tows

visual_sync.text_span: Slow and shift for responders, tows

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: When traffic and safety allow on a multi-lane road, how must you pass a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Putting an empty buffer lane between your mirrors and roadside officers prevents deadly shoulder sideswipes.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: What does South Carolina's move-over law require when heavy traffic makes changing lanes unsafe?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Never force a reckless merge into another car; drop to a safe crawl and pass with extreme care.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: What two law-enforcement reasons prompt an officer to initiate a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Blue lights might stem from a traffic infraction or a broader area investigation, so cooperate calmly.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: What three immediate steps should you take when police lights flash behind your car?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Flipping on your turn signal tells the officer immediately that you see the lights and are pulling over.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Once pulled over for an officer, what do you do with the engine, radio, hazards, and doors?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Jumping out of your car unasked looks confrontational; kill engine and music, hit hazards, and stay seated.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: What extra switch should you flip right after stopping for an officer at night?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Lighting up your cabin right away eases tension when the patrol car's spotlight hits your back glass.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Where do your hands belong during a traffic stop, and what must passengers do?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Visible hands on the steering rim and belted, still passengers keep the roadside encounter calm for everyone.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Why shouldn't anyone touch phones or rummage for papers before the officer speaks to you?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Ducking toward a glovebox or center console as an officer walks up mimics reaching for a weapon.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: When must you tell an officer about weapons inside the vehicle, and what applies to CWP holders?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Upfront disclosure at first greeting—following CWP protocol if licensed—prevents dangerous surprises mid-stop.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: If stopped by someone in an unmarked vehicle or plain clothes, what may you politely request?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Legitimate plainclothes or unmarked officers carry official agency identification and expect polite verification requests.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: How should you handle an officer's request for license, registration, and insurance when they sit out of reach?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Telling the officer your registration is in the glovebox and waiting for permission keeps every hand move expected.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: If an officer directs you to exit your car, what two safety habits apply?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Stepping well away from passing highway lanes while keeping empty hands visible protects both of you.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: Where do you challenge a traffic ticket you believe is wrong, and what should you avoid roadside?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders never overturn tickets; traffic court is the legal forum built to hear your side.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: Does taking a traffic citation from an officer legally count as admitting guilt?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Receiving the paper citation simply acknowledges notice of the charge and court date, preserving every defense.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: How do accepting a ticket roadside and contesting the charge in court work together?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Taking the ticket peacefully gets you safely off the shoulder while saving your legal challenge for the judge.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Compare South Carolina's rule on signing a traffic ticket with what can happen in other states?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: South Carolina citations require no driver signature, yet refusing to sign out of state can get you arrested.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Under what legal standard may an officer search your car without a court-issued warrant?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Under the automobile exception, probable cause that a crime occurred authorizes an immediate roadside search.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: What two safety and legal realities make fleeing law enforcement a disastrous mistake?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Running turns a minor traffic stop into a life-threatening pursuit carrying penalties far worse than any ticket.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: How and where should you report an officer who you believe acted improperly during a stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Check the citation—or ask politely—for the officer's name and department, then contact that agency promptly afterward.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: What four emotional and physical boundaries must you keep even if you or passengers face arrest?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Interfering with a passenger's arrest or resisting physically stacks criminal charges onto everyone involved.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: In what kind of driving environment must you stay extra alert for slow-moving vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Cresting a rural hill at highway pace can put a crawling tractor right in your lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: What speed ceiling and vehicle types does a reflective orange-and-red rear triangle warn you about?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Spotting that glowing orange-and-red emblem on farm, work, or horse-drawn rigs means closing speed is extreme.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: Why shouldn't you assume a tractor or combine operator on a rural highway knows you are behind them?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Heavy diesel roar blocks out road noise, so slow down before passing farm gear that might turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: What road rights and responsibilities apply to horseback riders and animal-drawn vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Riders and buggies share full legal roadway access while remaining completely unprotected in any impact.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: What noises must you avoid near horses or buggies, and what sudden move should you anticipate?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Horns or revved exhaust spook horses into bolting, and buggies turn left into farm lanes without blinkers.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: Contrast how noise affects passing a farm combine versus passing a horse-drawn wagon?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Combines are too loud for the driver to hear you, whereas horses hear everything and panic at horns.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: What three corner elements must you scan for before initiating a turn, and how do you alert others?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Sweeping every corner for signs, pedestrians, and vehicles before flipping your blinker catches conflicts early.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Which lane must you move into and hold before making a turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Turning across an adjacent through lane blindsides drivers traveling straight beside your quarter panel.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes while steering around a corner?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Your hands naturally steer where your eyes lead, so looking far along your target path smooths the arc.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Which wide steering habit must you avoid right before turning right?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Swinging left before a right turn fakes out trailing drivers into thinking you are changing lanes left.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: From which exact side of your lane should every right turn begin?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Hugging the right-most edge of your lane closes the curb gap so nobody squeezes inside your turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Whom must you yield to on a left turn, and from which side of your lane do you start?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Hugging your lane's far-left edge opens sightlines past opposing left-turners while letting through cars clear.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Compare your starting position inside the lane for a right turn versus a left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Right turns hug the right-most edge and left turns hug the left-most edge, making both easy to pair.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: At intersections where two or more lanes turn together, what lane rule applies mid-turn?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Drifting wide into the neighboring turn lane mid-corner clips the car turning right alongside you.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: What three speed, blinker, and mirror steps complete a safe turn?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Building pace smoothly, confirming a silent blinker, and checking rear mirrors blends you cleanly into new flow.
sec09-card-sec09-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Accelerate smoothly, cancel signal, check rear

visual_sync.text_span: Accelerate smoothly, cancel signal, check rear

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What roadside openings does a two-point turnabout use, and when do you choose it?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Using a driveway or alley turns you around cleanly whenever circling the block is impractical or impossible.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: How do you signal, stop, check, and position your rear bumper to start a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Pulling past the driveway first so you back into it lets you drive forward when re-entering street traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How do you work the steering wheel while backing slowly into the driveway during a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Turning sharply right swings the tail neatly in, and straightening wheels centers the car squarely before stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: What gear, traffic check, signal, and turn complete a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Finishing nose-out lets you scan left and right clearly before signaling left into your new lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: How do you set up and pull into an alley or driveway at the start of a forward two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Easing toward the road center and hugging the driveway's left side leaves swing room for backing out right.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: How far into the driveway do you pull on a forward two-point turnabout before shifting to reverse?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Pulling just far enough for your rear bumper to clear the curb sets up your controlled right-hand back-out.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Walk through backing out and driving away at the end of a forward two-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Backing out into the nearest lane puts blind-spot exposure at the end, requiring slow wheel control and blinker checks.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Contrast a two-point turnabout against a three-point turn in whether driveways or side streets are used?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Road-test examiners mark errors if you dip into a driveway during a scored three-point turnabout.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: Under which three street-width, block, and traffic conditions is a three-point turnabout appropriate?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Stopping sideways across both lanes belongs strictly on quiet two-lane streets where U-turns or block loops cannot work.
sec09-card-sec09-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Too narrow, no block, quiet two-lane

visual_sync.text_span: Too narrow, no block, quiet two-lane

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: What safer turnaround beats attempting a three-point turnabout on a busy city street?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Four easy corner turns around a block beat blocking fast two-way traffic sideways mid-street.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: Which three surface or boundary mistakes disqualify a clean three-point turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Keeping all four tires cleanly on pavement between the curbs proves tight steering control on your road test.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What mirror, signal, and curb-side stop open step one of a three-point turnabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Starting tight against the right edge gives your front wheels maximum turning radius across the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: After stopping at the right edge, what signal, blind-spot check, and steering move make up step two?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Glancing over your left shoulder catches overtaking cars before swinging perpendicular across both lanes.
sec09-card-sec09-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Left signal, shoulder check, hard left

visual_sync.text_span: Left signal, shoulder check, hard left

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: During step three's backing leg, how must you check for traffic and which way do you turn the wheel?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Looking over both shoulders instead of trusting the rearview mirror spots cars approaching from either side.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How do you complete step four of a three-point turnabout and resume normal travel?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Checking traffic and blind spots one final time lets you pull cleanly into the right lane with signals off.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: As you near any intersection, what speed adjustment and five-part visual scan should kick in?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Trimming speed early buys time to read signs, cross traffic, walkers, cyclists, pavement flaws, and blocked sightlines.
sec09-card-sec09-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Ease speed; scan controls, users, blind-spots

visual_sync.text_span: Ease speed; scan controls, users, blind-spots

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Why is counting on other drivers to obey stop signs or red lights a dangerous habit?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Defensive drivers verify others are actually slowing because you never steer or brake someone else's car.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Even when priority rules favor you at a corner, what readiness keeps you out of crashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Keeping an escape plan or brake margin saves your bumper when another road user ignores right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: After coming to a full stop at an intersection, what head-turn sequence spots cross traffic and bikes?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Checking left a second time confirms the nearest lane you cross first stayed clear while you looked right.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: Why shouldn't you stomp the gas the instant a red light flips green?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Checking for late red-light runners and clearing walkers prevents classic split-second green-light T-bones.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: How large a traffic gap must you wait for before crossing straight over or turning onto a road?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Small gaps trap you mid-crossing or force fast main-road traffic to slam brakes behind your slow turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: When sizing up a tight lane or turn, should you expect other motorists to scoot over and share room?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Assuming another driver noticed you and will drift aside invites sideswipes when they hold their lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Why must you wait to see an approaching car actually turn rather than pulling out on its blinker alone?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Approaching drivers often signal early for a driveway past you or cruise straight with a forgotten blinker.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: How do directional crossovers inside a diverging diamond interchange simplify left turns onto ramps?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Shifting traffic temporarily eliminates turning left across oncoming straight lanes, removing the riskiest ramp conflict.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: Between the two signalized crossovers of a DDI, which side of the road carries cross-street traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Following channelized lanes onto the left side between signals lets ramp left turns peel off conflict-free.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: How does a diverging diamond interchange compare with a conventional diamond on ramp turns and conflict points?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Eliminating opposing cross-traffic lefts streamlines interstate access and slashes vehicle-to-vehicle conflict points.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Along with reducing total conflict points, how does a DDI change the crashes that could still occur?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Removing high-angle T-bone crossing paths means any remaining contact happens at gentler, lower-speed angles.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Which two high-risk maneuvers does a restricted crossing U-turn intersection eliminate from side-street approaches?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Blocking side-street drivers from shooting straight across fast divided highways prevents deadly broadside crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: How does a cross-street driver go left or straight across a divided highway at an RCUT?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Turning right with flow first and looping through a dedicated one-way median opening splits judgment into one direction at a time.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: Which four types of traffic control devices can manage movements through an RCUT intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Whether signed with yield, merge, stop, or full traffic lights, the right-then-median-U-turn pattern stays identical.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: What overall safety result do RCUT intersections deliver on multi-lane corridors?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Replacing multi-lane broadside crossings with right turns and protected U-turns sharply cuts collision risk.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: Around the center island of a roundabout or traffic circle, which direction does traffic circulate and who yields?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Keeping right of the center island spins every car counterclockwise while incoming approaches wait for gaps.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: How should you adjust speed when nearing a roundabout or traffic circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Heeding advance roundabout warning signs and easing speed lets you judge circulating gaps smoothly.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Walk through the four steps from reaching a roundabout yield line to taking your exit?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Signaling right just before your exit tells waiting drivers at the next leg they can pull in.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Between a driver waiting at a roundabout entrance and a driver already circling inside, who holds priority?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Stopping inside a roundabout to wave someone in breaks circle rules and triggers rear-end chain reactions.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: Eliminating which two deadly crash types makes roundabouts safer than traditional four-way intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Curved one-way circle geometry physically prevents high-speed T-bone broadsides and nose-to-nose left-turn impacts.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: Which flashing light colors or side equipment on a stopped or stopping school bus command you to stay stopped?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: South Carolina requires stopping for flashing amber bus lights while the bus slows, not just flashing red.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: In South Carolina, may you hurry past a slowing school bus whose amber lights are flashing before red starts?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Unlike many states where amber merely warns, South Carolina treats flashing amber on a stopping school bus as a stop command.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: Once school bus lights go dark and the stop arm retracts out of sight, how should you proceed?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Young riders sometimes drop papers or dart back toward the bus right after the arm folds in.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: On a two-lane South Carolina road, which directions of traffic must stop for a stopped school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Students cross both lanes of a two-lane road, so oncoming and trailing drivers alike must halt completely.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: On a four-lane or wider multi-lane South Carolina highway, which direction must stop for a school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: South Carolina limits multi-lane bus stops to vehicles traveling behind the bus because riders do not cross four lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: Contrast oncoming drivers' school-bus duty on a two-lane road against a four-lane or multi-lane highway in South Carolina?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Knowing South Carolina exempts opposing traffic on any multi-lane highway, not only raised medians, beats a major test trap.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: What must you do if a school bus ahead activates red or amber flashing lights just as you try to overtake it?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Trying to squeeze around a bus once amber or red signals flash breaks South Carolina's mandatory stop law.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: Under what dual condition may traffic pass a stopped school bus without stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Only a dedicated passenger bay completely off travel lanes where pedestrian road-crossing is barred waives stopping.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Which everyday vehicles fall under a South Carolina Class D license, and what gross weight ceiling applies?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Regular family cars and pickup trucks stay on Class D until gross vehicle weight tops twenty-six thousand pounds.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Which vehicle weight figure decides the South Carolina license class needed, and where does Class D top out?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Checking the gross vehicle weight or rating on the doorplate tells you immediately whether Class D suffices.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Which South Carolina license class covers heavy non-commercial single-unit vehicles like large motor homes?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Personal motor homes or farm-use trucks over twenty-six thousand pounds need Class E rather than a commercial CDL.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Which license class covers non-commercial vehicle combinations topping twenty-six thousand pounds, like a motor home towing a car?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Hitching a heavy trailer behind an RV pushes a non-commercial rig past twenty-six thousand pounds into Class F.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How do South Carolina's Class E and Class F licenses split non-commercial vehicles above twenty-six thousand pounds?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Both share the same twenty-six-thousand-pound non-commercial floor, splitting strictly on one unit versus towing.
sec01-card-sec01-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Single unit E, hitched combo F

visual_sync.text_span: Single unit E, hitched combo F

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Which smaller rides may Class D, E, and F drivers operate automatically, and which sidecar setup stays off-limits?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: A two-wheeled motorcycle with a detachable sidecar still behaves like a motorcycle and requires Class M.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What minimum age and testing steps apply when getting South Carolina's Class G moped license?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Class G skips the on-road skills exam completely, testing only eyesight and written road rules at fifteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Does someone holding a valid license or permit in one of the other four classes need Class G to ride a moped?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Class G exists only for riders without another active South Carolina permit or license.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Which two-wheel and three-wheel machines fall under South Carolina's Class M license?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Whether a two-wheel bike runs solo, bolts on a detachable sidecar, or rolls on three wheels, Class M covers it.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Contrast how another valid license class treats riding a moped versus riding a two-wheel motorcycle?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Holding Class D lets you hop on a moped legally, yet riding a two-wheel motorcycle without Class M gets ticketed.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How is someone licensed if they drive both a car and a motorcycle, and what testing earns it?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Instead of carrying two plastic licenses, you pass both driving tests and carry a single dual-endorsed card.
sec01-card-sec01-R04.must_match_memory_hook: One card endorsed after both tests

visual_sync.text_span: One card endorsed after both tests

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What combined weight rating and towed-unit rating trigger a Class A commercial driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Both numbers must hit together—twenty-six thousand one pounds combined AND a towed unit topping ten thousand.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Which heavy single vehicles—and what light-trailer limit—fall under a Class B commercial license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Dump trucks and transit buses at twenty-six thousand one pounds stay Class B as long as any trailer stays at ten thousand or below.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which two passenger-count or cargo-placard uses place a smaller commercial vehicle into Class C?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Even a lighter shuttle van or pickup needs a Class C CDL once built for sixteen occupants or placarded hazmat.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: Why is Class C unique among the three commercial license classes?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Classes A and B hinge on pound ratings, whereas Class C hinges on carrying crowds or hazardous loads.
sec01-card-sec01-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Defined by cargo, passengers, not weight

visual_sync.text_span: Defined by cargo, passengers, not weight

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: How many valid driver's licenses may one qualified person hold at once?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Keeping multiple active licenses across classes or states is illegal; endorsements stack onto one card.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Which three documents matching your vehicle class must be with you whenever you drive or risk a fine?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Missing any one of those three items during a roadside check exposes you to a citation.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Which five facts must a U.S. citizen prove with original documents under Form MV-93 for a first SC card?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Bringing photocopies instead of originals from the MV-93 checklist stalls a first-time counter visit.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Where does a non-U.S. citizen apply for a South Carolina credential, and which checklist form governs?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Not every SCDMV office handles international verification, so pick a designated branch with Form MV-94 in hand.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Who must begin with a South Carolina beginner's permit, and what age and tests unlock it?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Every brand-new driver starts at fifteen or older by clearing vision screening and the written knowledge test.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Between six in the morning and midnight, who must sit beside a beginner's permit driver?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: A newly licensed twenty-one-year-old still falls short until they hold at least one full year of driving experience.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: How do supervision rules tighten if a beginner's permit holder drives past midnight?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: An ordinary twenty-one-year-old friend cannot supervise after midnight unless they appear on the statutory guardian list.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Compare who may supervise a beginner's permit from six in the morning to midnight versus after midnight?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Midnight flips supervision from any experienced twenty-one-plus driver over to South Carolina's approved adult list.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: Counting from the day you get your beginner's permit, what is the earliest day you can apply for a license?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Because you must hold the permit MORE than one hundred eighty days, day one hundred eighty itself is one day too early.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: How many total and nighttime practice hours must a fifteen- or sixteen-year-old permit holder log with an approved supervisor?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Logging ten dark-hour drives inside your forty prepares you before daytime-only conditional limits ever lift.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: What notarized permission and filing step let another responsible adult serve as item seven on the teen supervisor list?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Verbal parent approval is not enough; item-seven adults need notarized permission from items one-to-six on file with SCDMV.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: What two written steps let someone approved by the Department of Social Services supervise teen driving practice?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Youths in state care stay on track once written Social Services approval is delivered to the SCDMV.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: How long must a first-time applicant aged seventeen or older hold a beginner's permit before skills testing for full privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Turning seventeen skips teen curfew stages, yet first-time drivers still owe more than one hundred eighty permit days.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Beyond holding a permit past one hundred eighty days, which three extra requirements apply to fifteen- and sixteen-year-old applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Younger teens pair their permit calendar hold with formal driver ed, satisfactory school attendance, and forty practice hours.
sec01-card-sec01-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Driver ed, school standing, logged hours

visual_sync.text_span: Driver ed, school standing, logged hours

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: How many classroom hours and behind-the-wheel driving hours make up South Carolina's required teen driver's education?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Both parts must be passed—eight hours learning theory in class and six hours behind the wheel.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Which three school-status requirements must a fifteen- or sixteen-year-old meet to get licensed?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Skipping classes or facing suspension or expulsion at school stalls teen driver licensing too.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What three things does Form PDLA certify for teens, and who issues the form?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Your driver's education provider hands out Form PDLA once you pass, bundling school, course, and practice sign-offs.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: Which teen ages fall under South Carolina's graduated driver's license program, and how is it structured?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Starting with tighter night and passenger rules gives teens low-risk solo miles before full freedom.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: What narrow age bracket and two exams qualify a teen for a conditional license?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Hit fifteen and six months after holding your permit past day one-eighty and passing vision and skills opens conditional driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: When may a conditional licensee drive solo in standard versus daylight saving time, and when must an adult ride along?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Evening hours between six—or eight in summer—and midnight require a licensed twenty-one-plus adult beside you.
sec01-card-sec01-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Solo six-to-six or eight, adult midnight

visual_sync.text_span: Solo six-to-six or eight, adult midnight

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: How does daylight saving time shift the evening cutoff for solo driving on a conditional license?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Longer summer daylight adds two extra evening solo hours from six o'clock out to eight.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: How many under-twenty-one passengers may conditional or special restricted drivers carry solo, and what three exceptions apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Carrying a third friend under twenty-one requires a twenty-one-plus licensed adult unless everyone is family or commuting to school.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: What one-year record earns a conditional licensee full driving privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Staying free of both traffic tickets and at-fault crashes for twelve straight months unlocks full privileges.
sec01-card-sec01-F28.must_match_memory_hook: One year clean, zero at-fault wrecks

visual_sync.text_span: One year clean, zero at-fault wrecks

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: Who must supervise conditional or special restricted drivers if they drive between midnight and six in the morning?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Overnight driving never allows just any twenty-one-year-old passenger; only adults listed in state code qualify.
sec01-card-sec01-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Midnight to six needs statute-listed adult

visual_sync.text_span: Midnight to six needs statute-listed adult

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: What suspension hits a driver under seventeen who racks up six or more points within the first license year?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Even two moderate speeding tickets in year one can hit six points and park you for half a year.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: Which two paths qualify a sixteen-year-old under seventeen for a special restricted license?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Sixteen-year-olds enter either by testing fresh from a permit or stepping up from an existing conditional card.
sec01-card-sec01-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Pass tests sixteen, or hold conditional

visual_sync.text_span: Pass tests sixteen, or hold conditional

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does holding a conditional license connect once a driver turns sixteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: South Carolina links the fifteen-and-a-half conditional stage directly into the age-sixteen special restricted stage.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: How late does an approved waiver let a sixteen-year-old drive solo for work or extracurriculars, and what stays off-limits?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Even with an official work or activity waiver in your pocket, solo driving past midnight remains illegal.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Can a sixteen-year-old's evening waiver ever authorize driving solo at twelve-thirty in the morning?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Test distractors tempt you with late-shift exceptions past midnight, which South Carolina waivers never grant.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: Which forms, letters, screening, and fee are required at an SCDMV branch to get an evening waiver?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Note Form 447-CM must be signed in front of SCDMV staff alongside Form 447-NC, two letters, vision, and twenty-five dollars.
sec01-card-sec01-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Two forms, two letters, vision, twenty-five

visual_sync.text_span: Two forms, two letters, vision, twenty-five

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: Who writes each of the two explanatory letters required for a sixteen-year-old's driving waiver?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: SCDMV checks both sides—your employer, school, church, or coach confirms the schedule, and your parent approves.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: What two milestones grant a teen full driving privileges without even visiting an SCDMV branch?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Either celebrating birthday seventeen or finishing a ticket-free, at-fault-crash-free year upgrades you automatically.
sec01-card-sec01-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Turn seventeen or one clean year

visual_sync.text_span: Turn seventeen or one clean year

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: Compare the record-based route and the birthday route to full teen driving privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: A minor ticket delays the one-year clean upgrade, leaving age seventeen as the fallback milestone.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: What item does SCDMV mail when you earn full teen privileges, and how must you use it?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Driving late solo without keeping your card tucked inside that official SCDMV sleeve leaves full privileges unproven.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: Which three tests apply to an original license or class upgrade, and where can vision and knowledge be taken?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Every SCDMV branch handles vision and knowledge testing, even if road-test scheduling varies.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.question_text: Which single first-time license skips the behind-the-wheel skills test that every other class requires?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.teaching_text: Every car, truck, and motorcycle first license tests on the road; only Class G mopeds stop after vision and knowledge.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.question_text: Contrast the test lineup for a first moped license against every other original South Carolina license?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.teaching_text: Spotting Class G as the sole two-test outlier locks down easy exam questions on licensing steps.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.question_text: Who owes a road exam, and which two interchangeable names does the South Carolina manual use for it?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.teaching_text: Whether a question calls it the skills test or the driving test, both mean the exact same behind-the-wheel check.

sec01-card-sec01-F46.question_text: Which three subject areas appear on the knowledge exam, and what should glasses or contact wearers bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F46.teaching_text: Showing up squinting without your everyday glasses or contacts delays clearing the vision screen.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: Which three testing-room violations cause an automatic failure on the knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: Even stepping outside early or keeping a phone or tablet with you ends your knowledge test with a fail.
sec01-card-sec01-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Leaving, talking, or bringing devices, notes

visual_sync.text_span: Leaving, talking, or bringing devices, notes

sec01-card-sec01-F38.question_text: Which exams and license classes may third-party One Stop Driver Training and Testing Programs administer?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.teaching_text: Certified third-party schools can run knowledge and skills exams for first-time Class D and motorcycle applicants.
sec01-card-sec01-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Class D first-timers and Class M

visual_sync.text_span: Class D first-timers and Class M

sec01-card-sec01-F39.question_text: Even after passing with a third-party tester, what can SCDMV randomly require before issuing your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.teaching_text: Quality-control audits under state law mean any applicant can be picked to re-demonstrate skills at SCDMV.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.question_text: What is the examiner checking while riding beside you, and will they try to trick you into errors?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.teaching_text: Relax and drive normally because every instruction simply checks vehicle control and obedience to road rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.question_text: Who supplies the skills-test car, and which five safety items appear on the first inspection list?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.teaching_text: A cracked mirror or dead speedometer stops your skills test before you ever pull out of the stall.
sec01-card-sec01-F41.must_match_memory_hook: Supply car; lights, brakes, wipers, mirrors

visual_sync.text_span: Supply car; lights, brakes, wipers, mirrors

sec01-card-sec01-F42.question_text: Which four additional cabin controls and three vehicle credentials must your skills-test car also have?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.teaching_text: Check your horn, defroster, blinkers, belts, plate, registration, and insurance card in the driveway before leaving.

sec01-card-sec01-F43.question_text: What happens if your test car is unsafe versus if you forget to fasten your seat belt during the skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F43.teaching_text: A broken bulb reschedules your appointment, whereas rolling without buckling your belt puts a fail on your record.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.question_text: Distinguish the exact outcome of bringing an unsafe vehicle from driving unbuckled on skills-test day?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.teaching_text: Clicking your belt before shifting out of park avoids the easiest automatic failure on the entire exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F44.question_text: Which three items or people must accompany you when checking in for the skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F44.teaching_text: Make sure your liability insurer is licensed to do business in South Carolina and bring a licensed driver along.
sec01-card-sec01-F44.must_match_memory_hook: Prior card, licensed driver, SC insurance

visual_sync.text_span: Prior card, licensed driver, SC insurance

sec01-card-sec01-F45.question_text: Who is allowed inside or standing around the vehicle once the skills test begins?
sec01-card-sec01-F45.teaching_text: Family and friends wait away from the car so nobody coaches from the curb or rides in back.

sec01-card-sec01-F47.question_text: Along with controls, turns, signs, parallel and hill parking, how far do you back straight and what turnabout appears?
sec01-card-sec01-F47.teaching_text: Holding a dead-straight line in reverse for one hundred feet takes steady mirror and rear-window control.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Because starting procedures vary across vehicles, where should you check how to start yours?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Keyless fobs, clutch interlocks, and push buttons behave differently across models, so checking first prevents starter fumbles.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What three steps with your right foot, gear selector, and ignition start the engine safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Holding the brake while confirming park guarantees the car stays planted the instant the engine fires up.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Which gear position belongs to starting the engine, and when do you shift into drive?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Waiting until every pre-move scan is done before selecting drive prevents creeping forward unexpectedly.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Right after the engine starts running, which four types of dashboard warnings or gauges need a scan?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Catching low oil pressure, low fuel, or brake and air-bag alerts in the driveway beats stalling mid-traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What gear move and forward check come first when you prepare to pull away?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Confirming an open forward lane right as you select drive stops curb or parked-car bumps before rolling.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Along with looking ahead, which three zones around the vehicle require checks before moving?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Looking directly over your shoulder catches cyclists, pedestrians, or approaching cars hidden outside mirror angles.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What communication step comes right before moving your foot onto the accelerator to pull out?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Signaling before rolling alerts nearby drivers and cyclists that a parked car is entering the travel lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: How should your foot and heel press the accelerator to build speed smoothly?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Resting your heel on the floorboard anchors fine ankle control so the car accelerates without lurching.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: What must you check before moving your foot from the gas pedal to the brake?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Spotting a tailgater behind you lets you brake earlier and smoother so they do not slam your bumper.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: When slowing to a stop, which happens first between checking mirrors and moving your foot to brake?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Permit questions love flipping this sequence, yet knowing who follows closely shapes how firmly you can slow.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: What kind of foot pressure should stay on the brake pedal until the wheels stop turning?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Pumping or jabbing modern brakes jerks passengers forward and confuses drivers judging your deceleration behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Whether rolling forward or backing in reverse, which way do you turn the steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Overthinking reverse makes beginners crank the wrong way, whereas turning toward your desired path works both directions.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Where on the steering wheel should both hands rest, and how tight should your grip feel?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: White-knuckling the rim wears out your arms fast, while a balanced outside grip keeps steering responsive.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: How should your fingers and thumbs hold the wheel, and which grip is strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Grabbing the inside rim traps your wrist against spokes or a deploying air bag if a tire hits a pothole.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Using a clock face, which hour ranges mark proper placement for your left and right hands?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Dropping hands below the old ten-and-two habit keeps forearms clear of steering-hub air bags while boosting leverage.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: When is taking one hand briefly off the steering wheel acceptable while driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Shifting gears, flicking wipers, or flashing a hand signal takes a split second before returning both hands home.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Which three driver hand signals justify taking one hand off the steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Clear arm signals communicate turns and stops when sun glare or broken bulbs hide rear turn lamps.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What type of roadway should a new driver choose first when learning basic vehicle handling?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Low-traffic country lanes let beginners master steering feel and braking smoothness without multi-lane rush-hour pressure.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: What steering milestone shows you are ready to move on to practicing turns and parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Every straight road demands micro-adjustments, and mastering those builds the touch needed for tight parking spaces.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How does holding the wheel in the lower seven-to-nine and three-to-five zones improve lane keeping?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Relaxed shoulders stop tired arms from tugging down on the wheel and drifting across lane paint.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: At what speeds and in what maneuvers should you use hand-over-hand steering?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Crossing hands rapidly cranks tighter wheel angles needed at corners or stalls, whereas highway speed needs subtle inputs.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Where on the steering-wheel clock face do your left and right hands begin hand-over-hand steering?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Starting near the horizontal centerline gives both arms clean leverage before reaching into the upper rim.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Which sections of the wheel rim execute right and left hand-over-hand turns, and how do you straighten?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Working the upper third of the rim keeps pulls smooth and controlled, then unwinding mirrors the exact steps.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: In what two narrow situations does the manual allow steering with a single hand?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Cruising one-handed leaves you slow to recover if a blowout, gust, or sudden swerve hits.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: While one hand reaches briefly for wipers or lights, where must your steering hand stay?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Keeping your steering hand near the horizontal home zone prevents an accidental tug while flipping dashboard switches.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Which steering method shares the exact eight-to-nine and three-to-four clock zones used during a one-hand reach?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Linking both situations to eight-to-nine and three-to-four locks in one consistent home base on the rim.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What three safety reasons explain why at least one hand must stay on the wheel at all times?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Letting the wheel spin free or taking both hands off forfeits stability and risks painful spoke strikes.
sec06-card-sec06-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Keep balance, handle reversals, prevent injury

visual_sync.text_span: Keep balance, handle reversals, prevent injury

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: When is placing a hand at twelve o'clock on the steering wheel recommended?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Twisting your torso to look aft shifts your shoulder angle, making top-center the sole natural pivot for backing.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: In the manual's backing-up steps, which hand takes the twelve o'clock spot on the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Anchoring your left hand at the top frees your right shoulder and torso to rotate toward the back glass.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: What check must happen before climbing into the driver's seat to back out, and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Trunk lids and tailgates create a low blind zone that completely hides toddlers, pets, and bikes from inside.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: Once seated, what three actions with brake, gearshift, and left hand begin backing up?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Pinning the brake before selecting reverse stops driveway roll while your left hand sets up steering control.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: Where does your right arm go and where do your eyes look while reversing?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Bracing your right arm on the passenger seatback opens your chest so you see directly out the rear window.
sec06-card-sec06-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Right arm across, look out back

visual_sync.text_span: Right arm across, look out back

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: How should you use mirrors and a backup camera while reversing, and what zone do mirrors miss?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Staring only at glass or screens creates tunnel vision and leaves a blind pocket right behind your bumper.
sec06-card-sec06-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Glance briefly, mirrors miss directly behind

visual_sync.text_span: Glance briefly, mirrors miss directly behind

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: While backing up, what gives your main view and what role do mirrors and cameras play?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Examiners deduct points immediately if you reverse staring at a dashboard screen instead of looking out the back.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: How should you control speed in reverse, and why is creeping slowly essential?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Front wheels steer from the trailing end in reverse, so excess speed swings the car sharply off line.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: How much and in which direction should you steer when guiding a backing vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Small wheel inputs swing the rear bumper plenty, whereas big cranking motions send the front end wide.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: When turning while backing up, where else must you glance quickly besides straight back?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Turning in reverse swings your front fenders outward toward adjacent parked cars, mailboxes, or curbs.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: How long must you keep looking backward when finishing a reverse maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Facing forward while still rolling backward blinds you during the last few feet where curbs or pedestrians appear.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: What steering habit and visual habit stay consistent all the way through backing up?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Gentle wheel corrections paired with unbroken rear focus prevent last-second fender scrapes right before halting.
sec06-card-sec06-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Slight steering, eyes back until stopped

visual_sync.text_span: Slight steering, eyes back until stopped

sec02-m01.narration_text: Let's recap interstate and turnabout tasks plus the two-business-day, seven-calendar-day, and thirty-calendar-day retest waits. Wait two business days first. Keep business days first and calendar days next as you hit the quiz.

sec02-m02.narration_text: Quick pass through the forty-five-day new-resident switch, nine-month expired retests, and returning SC plates before dropping insurance. Forty-five days unless military, federal. Turn in there, SC cancels. Save yourself four hundred dollars in plate fees and jump into the quiz.

sec02-m03.narration_text: Time to review visitor home licenses, why an International Driving Permit is only a translation, and nine-month reciprocity. Valid home-state license covers visitors. Pair foreign licenses properly and crush the module quiz.

sec02-m04.narration_text: Let's run back free branch vision checks, thirty-six-month eye certificates, thirty-one-day military LES waivers, and Form 412-NC. Vision required, free branch screening. Months for eyes, days for military—step into the quiz.

sec02-m05.narration_text: Rapid check on eight-year citizen online renewals, the five-point cap, no back-to-back remote renewals, and never mailing cash. U.S. citizens earn eight years. Form 447-NC, vision, check, no cash. Your renewal rules are dialed in for the quiz.

hooks_spoken: Never drive; nine months skips tests
Cut in half after one year
sec02-m06.narration_text: Here is your quick review on the nine-month expiry cliff, half-off points after a year, and six-teen versus twelve-adult suspensions. Never drive; nine months skips tests. Cut in half after one year. Take that point-system mastery straight into the quiz.

sec02-m07.narration_text: Let's replay in-person eight-hour defensive driving once every three years, beating suspension start dates, and payment plans. Eight hours, post-ticket, once three-yearly. Keep those point-reduction rules sharp on the quiz.

sec02-m08.narration_text: Final review on the May 2024 DUI provisional cutoff, once-in-a-lifetime Form DL-127 route cards, and returning Temporary Alcohol Licenses. Six months, hundred dollars, ADSAP. Finish South Carolina Chapter two strong on the quiz.

sec03-m01.narration_text: Let's recap Form 447-SEL for males under twenty-six, the birthday-eighteen data transfer, and physical surrender before eighteen. Males under twenty-six complete 447-SEL. Keep twenty-six and eighteen clear as you step into the quiz.

sec03-m02.narration_text: Quick pass through red-heart donor cards, binding Anatomical Gift Act status, parent decisions under eighteen, and Donate Life SC. Joins registry, adds red heart. Those organ-donor rules are ready for the module quiz.

sec03-m03.narration_text: Time to review littering arrests, fines stacked with supervised pickup, cigarette butts, and keeping a trash bag inside. Littering brings arrest and fines. Keep wrappers and butts inside and crush the quiz.

sec03-m04.narration_text: Final review on golf carts—age sixteen with a license, SCDMV decals, four daytime miles, thirty-five-mile-per-hour roads, and specialty manuals. Sixteen licensed, SCDMV decal displayed. Finish South Carolina Chapter three strong on the quiz.

sec05-m01.narration_text: Let's run back cold tire gauge checks, doorframe numbers, and the Lincoln penny tread rule. Check monthly with pressure gauge. Your tire game is road-ready, so roll straight into the module quiz.

sec05-m02.narration_text: Quick rapid-fire pass on upright posture, the ten-inch chest gap, and ear-level head restraints. Back upright, both feet planted. Driver cockpit dialed in, now jump into the quiz and lock every point.

sec05-m03.narration_text: Time to recap your primary rearview mirror and both enhanced side-mirror setups. Interior windshield mirror leads rear. Blind spots shrunk and angles sharp, so knock out this module quiz.

sec05-m04.narration_text: Let's review South Carolina primary belt enforcement, strap placement, and how air bags team up. Pull over solely for unbuckled. Buckled low and snug, now head into the module quiz and crush it.

sec05-m05.narration_text: Rapid-fire check on rear-facing, forward-facing, booster, and fifty-seven-inch belt milestones. Under two rides rear-facing back. Seven and younger ride back. Every child passenger stage is crystal clear, so take on the quiz next.

sec05-m06.narration_text: Fast pass over misdemeanor loose-load fines, frame tie-downs, and securing pets. Misdemeanor fine plus cleanup bill. Nothing shifts or blows loose, so step into the module quiz and sweep it.

sec05-m07.narration_text: Final chapter recap on driver-assistance sensors, weather limits, and skills-check bans. Features assist, you stay focused. Pre-drive prep complete, so finish strong on this module quiz.

sec07-m01.narration_text: Let us run back South Carolina's First Car Rule, Same Time ties, and yielding from ramps or left turns. Never assume; read live conditions. Right-of-way rules are locked in, so jump into the quiz.

sec07-m02.narration_text: Quick fire drill on vertical versus horizontal signal colors, right-on-red stops, and flashing beacons. Red next; stop and wait. Traffic signal procedures are sharp, so go clear the module quiz.

sec07-m03.narration_text: Here is your rapid recap of yellow warning diamonds, fluorescent school alerts, and curve-and-merge signs. Yellow diamond with black markings. Warning sign recognition is dialed in, so crush the quiz next.

sec07-m04.narration_text: Time to review round yellow RR signs, white crossbucks, nonstop rail crossings, and blue emergency numbers. Advance rail; slow, look, listen. Railroad crossing rules hold zero traps now, so take on the quiz.

sec07-m05.narration_text: Final check on orange work-zone signs, mandatory flaggers, channeling panels, and temporary stop lines. Orange diamonds-rectangles with black. Chapter seven is complete, so finish strong on this quiz.

sec10-m01.narration_text: Let's lock in South Carolina's four-lane oncoming school-bus exception versus always stopping from behind. Behind a bus, always stop. Jump into the quiz and nail every school-bus stopping scenario.

sec10-m02.narration_text: Time for a rapid run through placard rules, eighteen-inch curb limits, and crisp angle-stall exits. Use designated parking areas always. Take those clean stall and curb numbers straight into the quiz.

sec10-m03.narration_text: Here is your quick check on bumper-aligned parallel turns, eighteen-inch finishes, and door-past-bumper exits. Spot space, check traffic, signal. Hit the quiz and crush every parallel-parking step.

sec10-m04.narration_text: Let's review downhill-right, curbless-right, and the lone uphill-curb street-center wheel cut. Turn right, except left one-way. Step into the quiz and own every hill-parking question.

sec10-m05.narration_text: Quick recap on mirror-then-shoulder checks, ramp acceleration speed, and braking inside deceleration lanes. Mirrors first, then shoulder check. Open the quiz and show smooth highway entry and exit control.
